title: sse-frag-hedge-and-toolcall-lease-to-prevent-partial-json-starvation
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: we observed a class of customer-visible failures where SSE fragments that contained the tail of a JSON object (e.g. end of a tool call payload) were dropped or emitted out-of-order under transient backpressure, producing partial JSON at the client and broken OpenAI-compatible toolcall handoffs. This PR introduces two complementary guards: (1) a fragment hedging timer that holds small tail fragments for a configurable window and attempts reassembly before emitting; (2) a lightweight toolcall leasing mechanism that quarantines toolcall sentinel events until their JSON spans are validated or a safety timeout elapses. Goals: reduce partial-JSON starvation, preserve event ordering for function/tool calls, avoid increasing steady-state latency for healthy streams. Implementation notes: - New hedging buffer lives at the streamer output layer; it tracks fragment anchors and a short timer (default 30ms) to allow late-arriving bytes to be coalesced. Hedging is adaptive: it uses recent reorder/latency metrics to shrink/expand the window. - Toolcall lease inserts a synthetic lease token for any tool/function sentinel (OPENAI "tool_call" style) and defers downstream handoff until either the hedger confirms the JSON span or lease timeout (default 120ms) fires. - Introduces an SSE anchor header (X-SSE-Anchor) that marks the logical span id for debugging and metrics; it is optional and not sent to external clients unless debug mode is enabled. - Backpressure behavior: when internal queueing indicates saturation, the hedger will prioritize anchor-complete fragments and emit partials with explicit "incomplete":true flag in a compatibility envelope to preserve downstream parsers. Rollback plan: feature gated via streamer feature flag (sse_frag_hedge_v2); can be disabled remotely. Test plan: unit tests for hedger state machine, deterministic reorder/integration tests with synthetic delayed segments, end-to-end with openai-compat layer using function call emulation, and perf benchmarks to confirm <5% P95 latency regression under normal load. Documentation: added notes and config knobs in docs/notes/streaming-frag-hedge.md. This description is a single continuous string (sections separated by hyphens).
commits: feat(sse): implement hedging buffer and adaptive window
feat(sse): add toolcall lease state machine and sanity timeouts
refactor(openai-compat): wire lease handoff into toolcall pipeline
test(sse): add integration tests for reordering and partial-json recovery
docs: streaming hedger behaviour and config knobs
review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Nice approach. Two high-level asks: (1) can we make the default hedging window configurable per-tenant? (2) need a fail-safe that avoids head-of-line blocking if many anchors are incomplete.
Maya Chen: Answered — made window per-tenant via StreamerConfig and introduced an eviction policy that escalates oldest anchors with an 'incomplete' compatibility envelope to avoid HOL blocking.
Priya Kapoor: Please add explicit metrics for hedger_emits/{coalesced,forced_partial,timeout} and toolcall_lease/{granted,expired}. We should also expose a debug sampling mode.
Maya Chen: Added metrics and an optional debug sampling flag documented in the config. Also added X-SSE-Anchor header (disabled by default).
Liam O'Connor: Integration tests look good. One nit: increase lease timeout to 120ms to accommodate high-latency inter-region spikes (suggested by earlier incident logs).
Maya Chen: Increased default lease timeout and added adaptive backoff when consecutive expirations are observed.
merge_commit_summary: sse: hedging buffer + toolcall lease to reduce partial JSON and stabilize function handoffs
release_notes:
- Introduce SSE fragment hedger to reduce partial JSON emission under transient reordering/backpressure.
- Add toolcall lease mechanism to preserve function/tool call ordering and avoid broken handoffs.
- New optional debug header X-SSE-Anchor and metrics for hedger/toolcall leasing.
- Feature gated; rollout controlled via streamer flags.
tests_run: perf: microbench streaming P95 under baseline and hedging enabled (P95 +3%)
notes_on_backport: Backport recommended to release/1.12 for customers who ran into partial-JSON incidents; hedging default disabled on older branches to avoid regression risk.
